newsitem.title: MEXICO: One Mexican crude port reopened, two shut in winds.
newsitem.headline: One Mexican crude port reopened, two shut in winds.

text.p: Mexico crude shipping port Cayo Arcas in Campeche state reopened at 0813 local/1413 GMT Friday after an almost 10-hour closure amid strong winds, a Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) port officials told Reuters.
The state-owned oil and gas monopoly's largest shipping port shut at 1835 local/0235 GMT, the official said.
The two other main crude ports along the Gulf of Mexico remained closed Friday, port officials said.
Dos Bocas port captain Jorge Rojano Rodriguez said the Tabasco state port was expected to be closed for oil shipments all day, as waves were 12 to 15 feet high.
At Pajaritos in Veracruz state, waves of up to 12 feet high kept the port shut, although winds had died down to 10 km per hour, a port official said.
A cold front moving southeast along the Gulf of Mexico has shut many of the nation's ports in the region and brought waves up to 60 km per hour.
